A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TARO study. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary Sections A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original VGGSound and Landscape evaluations, a subjective user study, ablations and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, subjective user study, ablations and qualitative comparisons, including supplementary results.

M1.justification: The flow-based transformer, onset-aware conditioning, timestep-weighted representation alignment, projection mechanism and inference procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3–4.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on VGGSound and perform zero-shot evaluation on Landscape. The user-study coverage and qualitative examples are also retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 12 retain SpecVQGAN, Im2Wav, Diff-Foley, See & Hear, FoleyCrafter, Frieren and MDSGen. Encoder and temporal-feature comparators also remain unchanged; newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, preprocessing, training settings, sampling procedure, metrics and user-study design are unchanged. Table 12's corrected Onset AP header matches the metric already listed in v2's supplementary Section D, establishing a labeling correction rather than a changed evaluation metric.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component, weighting, projection, encoder and injection-depth ablations, temporal-feature comparison, training-efficiency analysis and qualitative case studies in Section 5.3 and supplementary Sections C–F.

E5.justification: Both report the same MOS confidence intervals and specify 95% confidence intervals in Section 5.1. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, significance tests or other uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted or qualitative results are retained throughout. For example, Table 1 reports TARO FD 0.47, FAD 0.94 and alignment accuracy 97.19% in both versions. Table 12 changes only the mislabeled header, preserving every score.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation, interpolation schedules, AdaLN equations, alignment weighting and projection equations remain mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same TRA/OAC contributions and claims about fidelity, synchronization and efficiency, including the same headline performance figures.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations retain their meaning. Supplementary Section E preserves the limitations concerning dataset scale, fixed video duration, human speech and dependence on onset-detection accuracy.

D1.justification: Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, preprocessing and subjective-evaluation details remain unchanged. The abstract's code-access statement and supplementary Section A's project-page disclosure are also retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds five references: Masked Autoencoders, ITA-MDT, Predictive Coding for Decision Transformer, rating-based reinforcement learning with vision-language feedback, and MM-Diffusion. These accompany brief contextual edits without substantially revising TARO's research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and grammar corrections, standardizes several figure references and adds a funding acknowledgment before the bibliography. The main narrative and supplementary organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 12 replaces its second Onset Acc header with Onset AP. Printed page numbers are removed and reference text reflows, while all figures and tables retain their substantive displays.

improvement.justification: Correcting Table 12's duplicate Onset Acc header to Onset AP resolves an ambiguity and aligns the table with the metric list already present in v2. Small grammatical corrections also improve readability. These are limited reporting improvements; the methods, experimental evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
